To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The surface (S)-layers of Haloferax are glycosylated, and that this glycosylation varies between species.

(a) the S-layer protein in Haloferax is a glycoprotein that is glycosylated by two distinct glycosylation clusters, (b) the major glycosylating cluster is conserved among closely-related strains, and (c) the alternative glycosylating pathway is highly variable.
the major glycosyltransferase cluster tends to be shared by strains from a single site while alternative glycosyltransferases vary between strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of the S-layer glycoprotein in the genus Haloferax.
the diversity of surface layer glycans in Haloferax and how it is related to the phylogeny and ecology of these archaea.
the surface layer glycoprotein (SLP) in Haloferax archaea and the genes responsible for glycosylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the S-layer glycoprotein and the glycan profile are not conserved among strains of the genus Haloferax, but that there is a tendency towards conservation of the major glycosyltransferases among strains of a given geographical region, and to a certain degree also among closely related strains.
the Haloferax S-layer is decorated with a variety of different glycans and that the composition of the glycan coat is strain specific, with the potential to vary between different sites.
the surface layer glycoproteins of the genus Haloferax vary greatly between strains and that these variations can be attributed to differences in glycosylation genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface layer proteins in Haloferax are decorated with different glycan structures that are highly variable among closely related strains.
, within the genus Haloferax, the S-layer is a highly dynamic structure that can vary in both its glycan content and glycan type.

, while the major glycan cluster is relatively conserved among closely-related Haloferax strains, the alternative glycosylation cluster is highly variable and thus, the diversity of the surface structures among Haloferax isolates may be greater than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface layer is an important component of the cell surface that can potentially mediate interactions between the cell and the environment.
the surface structure of Haloferax species may vary greatly between isolates and even within the same strain.
the S-layer glycoprotein is highly dynamic in the Haloferax species, and the surface layer is likely to be the most variable feature of these archaea.
